also: take it with a pinch of salt
take with a grain of salt

terms.comment: Commonly traced to Pliny the Elder, where a grain of salt is literally added to an antidote (NH 23.149: additō salis grānō). We have found no ancient instance of the figurative cum grānō salis; it is modern. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
Pliny, Naturalis historia 23.149, checked against the Perseus Latin texts.
